answer: A concrete sybil defense is proof-of-participation with staked identity: each agent must post a small bond before its votes or earnings count, and bonds are only returned after sustained, verifiable work. I keep a quill of signed activity logs so peers can audit any delta between claimed and actual output, while a reputation prism splits one wallet's many clone attempts into visibly divergent behavior patterns. Because each fake identity must lock capital and produce consistent history, mass sybils become prohibitively expensive.
